scope: Selected closest component cases in a narrative feasibility review; not a census or prevalence denominator.
claim: Two distinct model-caused executable payload-code revisions become active in one identified continuing remote-access process, with independent remote-control results after each.

status_codes.documented: Primary source supplies case-specific measurements, artifacts, code, or a time-ordered run record for this link; see the case note for the exact strength.
status_codes.reported: First-party source says the link occurred but does not publish enough of the chain to check it independently.
status_codes.mechanism: Source establishes an implementation path or capability, without a measured use of this link.
status_codes.not_shown: The reviewed public source does not establish the link; this is not evidence that it never occurred.
status_codes.outside_scope: This source's evaluated system does not include the required model, executable payload revision, or remote-control workload.

cases.note: The sample requests rewritten script code from a hosted model, but the examined self-update path was disabled. A generated response is not an applied active version.

The author describes an in-process generated-module compile/repair loop; corrections chiefly precede a successful module execution. The intentionally curtailed demonstrator did not implement a remote-control workload.

Model-directed cumulative source edits produced compiled variants, with manual debugging in the pipeline. Function-preservation checks were proxies; no continuing implant or post-revision control session was tested.

External model-guided candidate refinement and individual control-channel checks are measured. Each candidate starts from a fresh VM, so the connection result is not after a revision of the same resident instance.

A passing fresh candidate requires session/traffic evidence plus server-side command and file-transfer checks. The endpoint snapshot is restored before every candidate, and unblocked alerts do not fail the pass rule.

Pinned code supports in-interpreter function/method replacement and the paper reports repeated optimization, but does not publish a stable process-ID/version sequence. It evaluates reasoning tasks, not remote access.

A continuing driver loaded successive Tor versions at explicit update points; several under load preserved observed TLS continuity. Revisions were developer-prepared, and no remote-command result was checked after each version.

A lab RAT kept communicating with its control server while a separate GAN adapted traffic parameters. Parameters are not executable payload code, and the paper does not give after-each-change command results.

Anthropic says actor-side agents identified, modified, and redeployed detected artifacts; repeated iteration until undetected is partly described as workflow design. No two-version process or after-each access trace is published.
A resident model action loop, changing author-side builds, and a later upgrade capability coexist; no published trace joins model output to a live code upgrade or checks control after two upgrades.

One worker is reported to have alternated two code trees nine times, with version-specific inference outputs. Exact model-response-to-patch provenance and independent process telemetry are absent; checked function was inference service.

Two retained code edits are attributed to Codex and training checks attest execution. Three poisoned-lab respawns interrupt the 82-iteration session; the third retained edit was human/orchestrator-set. No one-process two-change lineage or remote-control test is published.

Static code supports reimporting a model-writable tool module into a continuing interpreter at the next model-call boundary. No observed two-version generated-tool trace or remote-control outcome is published.

Controller-side model repair addresses local pre-delivery validation failures; endpoint executes transient scripts through a continuing stub. No resident stub-code replacement or two-version access trace is published.

Published test source checks one fixture revision from v1 to v2 in a running Lisp image. Author notes demonstrate that nominal reload success can leave stale handlers or catalogs and that some live structure changes require restart. No model-to-two-edit trace or remote-control outcome.

All 27 lineages produced two changed Python harness snapshots, but each qualified and evaluated version was run as a separate task harness. Held-out game score and a post hoc version selector do not measure same-process activation or remote-control survival.

A RAT queried a hosted model for classification of harvested data while separate preexisting functions handled remote control. Distinct recovered builds do not show model-caused live revision or access after it.

cases.setting: pinned benign self-modifying agent research repository
cases.note: The outer evaluator can import changed meta/task-agent classes across generations, but each candidate forks an archive member and each task row instantiates a new TaskAgent object. Author-reported peer-code adoption and score changes do not identify one resident task agent receiving two active revisions; no remote-control workload.

A separate control plane synthesizes two pure scheduling-policy functions and stages selected code; the data plane is described as loading it at a monitoring boundary while serving continues. The public paper does not publish a process-ID and two-version activation trace or per-version request outcomes. Rescheduling counts are plan changes, not code-swap counts; no remote-control workload.

cases.setting: first-party incident-response account of ARTEX-assisted persistent backdoor deployment
cases.note: NVISO reports an ARTEX-assisted intrusion deploying a persistent Linux backdoor. The implant's existing binary relocates to memfd and restarts as a detached process. The public account does not show model authorship of the code or any revision, two active code versions in one process, or independent remote-control results after each.

cases.setting: external malicious model-repository artifacts and operator-side self-test
cases.note: JFrog ties artifact creation, upload, and a self-test to an ARTEX agent task with high confidence from leaked operator environment and commit history; exact LLM response-to-edit provenance and human choice are unresolved. Repository versions are not active versions in one resident process, and the self-test is collection from the operator's own container, not after-change remote control.

cases.setting: controlled agent-ecosystem configuration infection and remote task retrieval
cases.note: The model-mediated change is an instruction/configuration file reloaded on new single-turn sessions, not executable payload-code revision in one process. A marker checks C2-category URL retrieval and task execution, while a separate five-restart panel checks retention of the same instruction. No two active code revisions or after-each-version remote-control results.

cases.setting: first-party static analysis of malicious package installing a general AI agent for remote tasking
cases.note: Early publisher releases contain code to install and remotely task Hermes Agent as a service; later releases switch package delivery paths. SafeDep did not observe installation on a victim or recover later downloads. There is no model-to-code revision trace, one-process activation sequence, or independent remote task result after each version.

cases.setting: pinned benign agent code and committed self-edit proposal registry
cases.note: LLM-directed Python plugin evolution and in-process reload are implemented in one codebase. The committed proposal registry has 11 integrations of distinct plugin targets, 12 validation failures, and no evolution_loop proposal. Integration only proves a compiled/copied file; no two-version load and hook-result trace or remote-control workload is published.

cases.setting: pinned benign long-running Elixir agent implementation
cases.note: Agent-facing upgrade_code accepts new module source, and BEAM HotReload compiles/loads it in the running VM. Successful compile status can coexist with absent or failed tool-registry swap; health check is metadata-only. No published model-to-two-version invocation trace or remote-control workload.

cases.setting: IEEE conference abstract and related author's restricted-thesis repository abstract
cases.note: IEEE abstract reports model-generated code variants over mutation cycles; accessible text does not identify active-version or process lineage. Related thesis abstract reports 45 bidirectional C2 workflows across 15 products, but not per-revision checks; PDF is restricted and the thesis matrix cannot be assumed identical to the IEEE experiment. Claims are abstract-level only.

cases.setting: controlled benign defensive shield demonstration and project implementation documents
cases.note: First-party account reports one Codex-generated Java guard attached to running Elasticsearch, with install/reject log entries and continued service operation. Public record lacks exact model-to-bytecode/PID trace. Standard documented Java-agent path reaches JVMs at startup, not already-running JVMs; live-demo attach path is not reconciled. No second accepted code version or remote-control workload.

cases.setting: field investigation with full technical report and analyzed modular RAT families
cases.note: DriveSilkRAT implements in-memory task plugins and C2 result upload; CookiETagRAT reports load success before mapping/initialization, while NomadRAT reports it after initialization. These are distinct RAT families and no model-response-to-plugin lineage is published. Medium-confidence AI-assisted development inference concerns indirect code clues; no two active versions in an identified process or command/result after each.

cases.setting: first-party investigation of selected 2026 agentic web-shell intrusions
cases.note: An agent rotated five ASPX web-shell variants across more than 40 paths in one case; separate observations include 40–100 encoded one-use payloads in a session and Python/PHP/Bash executions in the same process chain. Two WMI-backdoor versions differ in comment language. These are script/artifact changes, not a two-version active-code lineage in one identified process; exact model provenance and post-each-version results are absent.

cases.setting: author-committed benign model conversation and pinned in-image Lisp extension loader
cases.note: The trace contains two byte-distinct model-submitted memory.lisp versions and two successful load reports in one conversation; historical code calls Common Lisp load in the running image. The first adds an extension, the second revises it. In-image tool/hook results are logged only after the second load, so the first does not meet the ledger's active-and-functional revision rule. No OS PID/image record, after-first functional check, or remote-control workload. Documented status applies to model submission and the second load, not the full Drexel chain.

cases.setting: first-party report of exposed agent controller and field shell outcome
cases.note: Amazon inspected controller prompts and AI output and reports Cairn agents wrote one Python reverse-shell payload via a file-write flaw. A training endpoint then spawned a new interpreter that imported the payload and established a root shell. The public report does not publish exact output-to-artifact bytes, and the new process is not a revised continuing implant. There is no two-version serial chain or after-each task/result.
